Subject: Order form: liability boundary - lost profits vs direct damages (initial)

Hi Sarah —

Following our call this morning, attaching an updated order form with redlines focused on the limitation of liability section. The main ask from Acme was clarity on what constitutes direct damages vs indirect/consequential (specifically lost profits, loss of data, and goodwill).

Quick summary of our proposed positions (see attached liability matrix):
- Cap: one year of paid fees for the order form (aligned with our standard)
- Exclusions: wilful misconduct, personal injury, and breach of confidentiality are excluded from the cap
- Consequential damages: carve out lost profits and third-party claims only where explicitly resulting from Redwood's certified breach — otherwise captured by cap

Can you confirm whether Acme's counsel will accept the language in section 5.2 (we converted their paragraph into illustrative examples to reduce ambiguity)? If not, please flag the exact lines so we can prepare counter-language.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redlines.docx, redwood-liability-matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Sean —

Thanks for the redlines and the matrix. Quick points from our side after a first pass:
- Acme needs lost profits to be an explicit exclusion from the cap for incidents causing prolonged platform outage (we will provide a short example scenario in the next email).
- Loss of data and loss of goodwill are trickier: our counsel prefers these to be outside the cap if they arise from Redwood’s failure to meet security obligations.
- We can live with a single-year fee cap for standard uptime/availability incidents, but want carve-outs for security breaches and gross negligence.

James is looping in counsel to draft specific carve-out language. Can your legal team share a short precedent paragraph that ties exclusions to defined security obligations (e.g., "material breach of Section 3 (Security and Data Protection)")? That helps us avoid circular definitions.

—Sarah
Sarah Patel

Team —

Short note from counsel: Acme will propose the following draft carve-out language for lost profits and loss of data as "excluded consequential damages" where the damages are a proximate result of a material breach of Redwood's security obligations. We will share exact wording tomorrow. Two asks for Redwood: (1) provide a narrowly tailored precedent paragraph that references the security section by section number (not circular), and (2) confirm that forensic and notification costs (e.g., breach response) are included in the security carve-out (or confirm if Redwood wants them to remain subject to the cap).

If Redwood wants to limit the scope, consider conditional carve-outs tied to (a) customer demonstrable loss (accounting/profit-and-loss) and (b) receipt of a final third-party adjudication. That is probably too restrictive for us, but we wanted to flag tradeoffs.

Regards,

James / Sarah —

Thanks for the input. Attaching a short precedent paragraph and an annotated example (see redwood-liability-matrix.xlsx) that ties the carve-out to a material breach of Section 3 (Security and Data Protection), and also proposes a narrowly scoped definition of "forensic and notification costs" that would sit in the carve-out. A few key points from Redwood legal and product that informed this:
- We can accept a security-linked carve-out for lost profits and loss of data, but only where (i) the customer demonstrates quantifiable loss using accounting records and (ii) Redwood's breach is the proximate cause.
- Goodwill is highly subjective — propose we keep it within the cap unless Acme can identify a quantifiable third-party claim tied directly to Redwood's breach.
- Forensic/notification costs: Redwood is willing to treat reasonable third-party breach response costs as excluded, capped at $250k per incident, and subject to mutual audit rights.

Proposed paragraph (in the attached doc) references Section 3.2(a) and adds three short examples to reduce disputes. If that looks acceptable to Acme, Vanessa (security lead) and Connor (contracts ops) are ready to do a quick 30-min call to finalize drafting.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
